headline: Europe buys the chip dip into Anthropic's debut while Hong Kong takes the curbs

findings.headline: The overnight chip sell-off flipped in Europe, but not in China
findings.body: European chipmakers led the rebound after Anthropic priced its IPO at $83, above its $70 to $78 range, with ASML, STMicroelectronics and Infineon up roughly 3-5% and Soitec up about 13% on a better fiscal 2027 forecast. Hong Kong went the other way because the new US export curbs land directly on Chinese AI: Tencent fell nearly 7% after a third-quarter revenue miss and a warning that the curbs may slow model training. The split says the AI hardware trade is now being priced by who can still buy the chips, so Anthropic's Nasdaq debut tonight is the test of whether the European bounce lasts.

findings.headline: Shenzhen summit ends with words, not a trade deal
findings.body: Trump, Xi and Putin finished their trilateral on Ukraine and nuclear arms without immediate statements, and China's four-point peace declaration offers nothing on trade. China's Commerce Ministry is still protesting the new US restrictions, and the US-China truce expires on 10 January 2027, so the chip-curb risk is unresolved. The one market-relevant line was Trump saying he and Xi both want oil to keep flowing through the Strait of Hormuz.

findings.headline: The ECB may drain liquidity alongside its next hike
findings.body: Reuters reports the ECB will discuss doubling banks' unremunerated minimum reserves from 1% to 2% next week and decide in December, which ING estimates would cut excess liquidity by about €175bn. That would tighten euro money markets on top of the hike already expected in December, after Wednesday's 2.6% core inflation print and Vujcic not ruling out more. Kocher and Panetta speak today, and four Fed speakers plus US jobless claims follow this afternoon.

view: Our view: the morning's AI sell-off has become a split, with Europe's chip suppliers bought on Anthropic and China's AI names sold on the curbs, rather than a reversal of the whole trade. The bigger slow-burn risk is policy: a December ECB hike plus a reserve drain would tighten euro funding just as the Fed leans hawkish.
